summary.headline: Aeroflex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72.4% YoY to INR145.97 crore, with EBITDA margin at 23.04% and SFN skid assemblies contributing INR32.4 crore (~23%).
summary.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR145.97 crore (+72.4% YoY), with EBITDA up 116% to INR33.5 crore and margin up 468 bps to 23.04%. PAT rose 162% to INR18.79 crore (about 13% margin). Growth came from flexible hoses (+41% YoY), assemblies and value-added products (faster), and the new SFN liquid-cooling skid assemblies for data centres. Management said sequential margin dipped due to ramp-up manpower costs for Taloja and Chakan facilities and West Asia-related logistics costs.

financial_highlights.change: more than +100% YoY; margin +278 bps YoY

segments.name: Flexible hoses and assemblies
segments.commentary: Hoses grew 41% YoY and assemblies grew faster. Mix was 63% fittings/assemblies and 37% plain hose; hose-only margins are 16-20% and assembly margins 22-26%.

segments.name: SFN skid assemblies (data centre liquid cooling)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.4 crore on 1,040 units in Q1, about 23% of revenue. Capacity expanded from 6,000 to 9,000 units/yr; target 15,000 units/yr by start of Q3 FY27. Management says skid margin is in line with company average.

segments.name: Metal bellows
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR3 crore in Q1. Management expects an uptick over the next two quarters; bellows utilisation is not yet at optimum.

segments.name: Hyd-Air
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR7 crore in Q1. Used internally for hose-assembly components, not sold to third parties; capex plan under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Company EBITDA margin target of 25% over the next few years; management says it is on track, but gave no quarterly margin guidance.
Flexible hose capacity to rise from 17.5 million m/yr to 20 million m/yr, to be completed by Q3 FY27; hose-related capex budget ~INR54 crore, with the remainder spent in FY27.
SFN skid capacity to reach 15,000 units/yr by expected Q3 FY27 (October-November, dependent on machine supplier delays); total skid capex budgeted at INR48 crore.
Q4 FY27 skid exit run-rate guided at ~60-65% utilisation on the 15,000-unit capacity (about 750 skids/month per analyst), which management said remains intact.
Optimal skid utilisation of ~80% expected in FY28, after a full year at 15,000 units.
Management cited a peak-utilisation potential of INR650-675 crore top line for flexible hose plus assemblies, assuming 70% of sales from assemblies.
Management said the SFN share of revenue would be discussed at year end, not quarterly; it did not reiterate the 25% share target.
capex_capacity: Flexible hoses: 17.5 to 20 million m/yr by Q3 FY27; current utilisation 65-66%.
SFN skids: 9,000 units/yr now, targeting 15,000 units/yr by start of Q3 FY27; some machines already commissioned, others arriving Q2 and Q3.
New Chakan (Pune) plant under setup; a new facility for hose assemblies for an international customer was also set up.
Hyd-Air capex plan for FY27 under discussion; to be announced once finalised.
Skid machines are largely fungible and can be redeployed to bellows or other flow-control applications (HVAC, ports, terminals).
demand_pricing: Export growth was 43% YoY; Europe (Italy, Spain, France, UK) and the US grew, including hose assemblies for European data-centre applications.
Skid assembly pricing varies by design. Management said the average value per skid is not a valid price metric and that margins are costed per design.
International skid competitors named: Senior and Parker, plus local players in the US and Europe. Management declined to name domestic competitors.
Largest US customer is the source of the fire-hose assembly for data centres, expected to be commercialised by end-Q1 FY28 with international supply; margin 23-26%.
Management said about 40-odd skids go into 1 MW of liquid-cooled IT load.
Customer dispatch schedules come about 2 months ahead; tentative Q3 project lists are also shared.
Logistics costs rose sharply due to the West Asia crisis, which began in mid-March and worsened through Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the flexible hose assembly business, and is it on track for 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Hose-only margins are 16-20% and assemblies 22-26%. The 25% target is for the whole company's blended EBITDA margin, not hose alone. Mix is 63% assemblies and 37% hose, so blended is about 22-23%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SFN average price per skid decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price per skid depends on design (piping length and content), so per-unit value is not a valid metric. It said margins are unaffected because each skid is costed separately.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the skid expansion from 9,000 to 15,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Total budgeted skid capex is INR48 crore for the expansion from 2,000 to 15,000. Some machines have arrived, others are planned for Q1 and Q2 FY28, and ancillary machines are used from day one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 exit run-rate of about 750 skids a month still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60-65% utilisation guidance on the 15,000-unit capacity remains intact, but the final Q4 plan depends on Q3 visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall 80 bps QoQ when skid volumes doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to added skid-team headcount, the new hose-assembly facility for an international customer, and higher logistics costs from the West Asia crisis. It asked to be judged on a YoY basis.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 employee-cost deleverage is one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the costs relate to ramp-up manpower at Taloja (SFN) and Chakan, and that bellows utilisation is still below optimum, so margins should improve as those ramp up.
